newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINE BAN FOR PARAGUAY KEEPER CHILAVERT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE BAN FOR PARAGUAY KEEPER CHILAVERT.

text.p: A judge banned fiery Paraguay captain Jose Luis Chilavert from playing professional soccer in Argentina for 13 months on Thursday for punching an employee of a rival soccer team during a match.

The tall, heavily-built goalkeeper was also given a three-month suspended jail sentence for punching a stadium assistant in the head in a game between Chilavert's team Velez Sarsfield and Gimnasia y Esgrima de la Plata in April 1994.

"I'm feeling calm, I have very good lawyers," Chilavert told Argentine television, "And if they ban me from playing sport, the ban will just apply here in Argentina. Argentina isn't the only place where they play soccer."
Chilavert, who scored from a free-kick against Argentina to clinch a draw for Paraguay in a World Cup qualifying match in Buenos Aires on Sunday, said he was being victimized for his nationality.
"They can't forgive me my success because I'm Paraguayan, but I feel more proud of that than ever," he said.

A menacing figure in goal who wears a bulldog design on his chest and thrives on intimidating opposing players, Chilavert is a national hero in Paraguay and was decorated by its government just weeks ago for his soccer prowess.
He has made much of being a dark-skinned Paraguayan who has succeeded in Argentina, a much richer country with a tradition of condescension towards its South American neighbors.
Chilavert, 31, snidely compared his sentence with the treatment of Argentina's veteran superstar Diego Maradona, still to be sentenced for shooting at a group of journalists with an airgun in 1994.

"Murderers, child-rapists, a person who fired a gun with telescopic sights at journalists...to this day they undoubtedly still haven't sentenced him. And they sentence me so quickly. It seems strange to me," he said.
Regarded by some as the best goalkeeper in the world, Chilavert helped his club win Argentina's last championship, saving a penalty in the match that clinched the league title.

Recently he has become known for his voodoo-like capacity to score from free kicks, including one 60 metres from goal in the last championship. In Sunday's match, the Argentine players looked visibly psyched out by the big Paraguayan, who booted an equaliser past rival goalkeeper German Burgos.
